title: Sprite stacking for 100+ buildings with AI: is there a workflow or skill that doesn't burn through tokens?
author: Perfect-Builder4321
selftext:
I'm a solo dev making a Three Kingdoms strategy game (working title: Three Kingdoms: Struggle for Tianxia) with a lot of AI help: Claude writes most of the code, and Codex draws the pixel art.



Right now every building is a single front-facing pixel sprite standing on a 3D ground. It looks fine until you rotate the camera, then the buildings are obviously flat. So I'm looking for a way to let buildings face different directions while keeping the 2D pixel look.



What I tried

\- Adding fake thickness to the existing sprites: no extra art, but it looks like thick cardboard from the side.

\- Front + roof + side images per building: 3 to 4 times the art, and the seams don't line up.

\- Voxels: the most 3D, but it stops looking like the same pixel game as my characters.

\- Sprite stacking: this one I like most. Each building is a sheet of horizontal slices, stacked and rotated. I built a test with about 30 slices per building, pre-rendered into 16 directions, so in game it's still one sprite and costs the same as now. It sits next to my 2D soldiers much better than voxels.



The problem is making the slices

I have 100+ building sprites. My test slices were generated by code, which works but loses the hand-drawn feel. Asking an image AI for 30 slices per building doesn't really work: every slice has to line up with the others, and if one is off by a pixel you get stripes. Drawing them one by one with AI, building by building, would eat a huge amount of tokens and usage, and I've already hit weekly limits on art jobs.



So my question:

\- Is there a skill, tool or workflow that turns existing front-view sprites (or one reference image) into stacking slices efficiently?

\- Has anyone had luck with AI making a voxel model first and then slicing it, or a script that slices a model into layers?

\- If you've done sprite stacking at scale, did you build every model by hand (SpriteStack, MagicaVoxel), or find a shortcut?

\- Any tips to keep token use down for a big batch like this, like generating a few base parts and reusing them across buildings?



Happy to share what I learn back here.

![img](o7kemtczd74i1 "Same two buildings four ways: my current AI-drawn front sprite, a voxel test, sprite stacking, and the stack pre-rendered (1 of 16 directions). The stacking slices are temporary, made by code.")

![img](p0l7yo30e74i1 "One slice sheet, any angle. This is what I want for 100+ buildings, without hand-making every model.")
